_comment: v3 weights. Values are RELATIVE, not required to sum to 1.0 -- composite.py normalizes by their sum. Full-weight categories are 0.15; Drought, Seismic and Air Quality are 0.05, i.e. each contributes one third of what a full-weight category does. Drought overlaps heavily with Wildfire/Heat's own signal in the same places; Seismic is a comparatively rare/localized threat nationally; Air Quality is chronic-exposure rather than acute-event risk, so it is deliberately a modifier rather than a driver.

_exponent._comment: Composite is a weighted power mean (Holder mean) with this exponent, not a plain weighted average -- see composite.py. p=1 would be a plain average; higher p makes categories that are ALREADY high contribute disproportionately more, so a place with several categories in the 90s scores much higher than a place with the same average made up of uniformly-moderate scores. p=3 was chosen empirically: it visibly fixes the 'Miami Beach scores ~23 despite Flood=99/Hurricane=96' problem from v1 without letting a single maxed-out category alone dominate the score (one category at 100 with everything else at 0 still only yields ~53, not ~100).
